audit: auditor 2: academic quality of 3_Final_Project_Report_Flood.docx (examiner view, master's AI course); read-only
inputs_read: ../Handin_2026-11-02/3_Final_Project_Report_Flood.docx (full text, tables and captions, in order)
overall: A rigorous, unusually honest piece of work with a clear finding. As a master's examiner I would give it a good grade, held back by four things. (a) Template and integrity gaps an examiner sees at once: the group number is blank, the repository and data links are still placeholders, the abstract is over the word limit, the literature is declared unread by any member, and the signed declaration does not match 0 of 4 team checks. (b) One verdict omitted by the project's own pre-fixed rule (E4e full model = CAUTION). (c) RQ2 counts as support a result that failed the pre-fixed rule. (d) Readability: the fixed wordings recur 10 to 33 times each, 29 sentences run over 60 words, and core acronyms are never expanded.

dimensions.reason: The gap is precise and measured (rain shares 18% / 35% / 47% around 611 onsets; median 4% against 50% for missed onsets). However, 'no published study, to our knowledge' rests on a narrow review (6 of 9 studies come from one group, and none on sub-daily or multi-timescale LSTMs or on operational warning verification).

1 aim, 4 objectives and 3 RQs with criteria fixed in advance, each answered in 9.1. However, the objectives are worded as deliverables, the RQ1 hypothesis does not match its question, the RQ3 hypothesis ('not yet') is not testable as worded, and 9.1 counts RQ2 as supported for E4e by a non-pre-specified paired count after the fixed rule failed.

Table 2 compares 9 studies by dataset, approach, key result and limitation, and the gap follows from it. However, the prose is only two paragraphs, metrics and baselines are not compared across studies, and Sections 2.2, 8.1 and 8.3 state that no team member has read the papers. An examiner will read that as an integrity and competence problem.

The work uses a time split by target day, 10 leak checks, matched-window controls, a seed rule with a Wilcoxon test, criteria fixed in advance and full disclosure of post-hoc choices (seeds 3 and 4, E1 follow-ups). Weaknesses: no Wilcoxon p-value is printed although the registry holds them; no multiple-comparison correction; 12 basins; the static-attribute overlap. 'No clear difference' sits next to a Wilcoxon p of 0.007 (E3 NSE) and a drop of 0.072 (E2 one-day NSE) without explanation.

GO is stated as not met, the E4b strict rule as not met, and the AORC hindsight and satellite-era caveats are in place. Errors: (i) the full E4e model's onset verdict is CAUTION by the fixed rule (CSI 0.47), yet the report says 'NOT YET ... in every set that could be had in practice' 6 or more times; (ii) the Table 5 AORC row prints +33.1 points beside the control of 18%, but +33.1 is the gain over lstm_wq and the gain over that control is +33.7; (iii) the two-hour E4e variant warns of 70.1% (the warned half of GO on its own) at 42% false, and the 42% is not stated; (iv) 'the information, not the network' is stated more generally than 12 basins and 4 model kinds support.

8.2 is complete and candid on scope, seeds, AORC, forecast, E4e and leaks. It ends with an unsupported claim ('these limits bound the numbers, not the direction'), does not discuss the statistical power of a 12-basin Wilcoxon test, and does not mention that the onset sets differ by lead.

Fixed wordings repeat until the text is hard to read: 'an analysis made after the fact' 33 times, 'an upper bound that cannot be had in practice' 28, 'hindsight at most about 4 points' 17, 'comparable only inside it' 16, the long Stage IV wording 10, 'not yet done' 12. 29 of about 530 sentences run over 60 words. NSE, POD/FAR/CSI, KGE, HUC, AORC and GEFS are never expanded in the body; pod, far and csi appear in lower case; 'Q95' is undefined. Internal jargon (hand-over x11, registry, critic passes, team.json, the Windows PC) and file paths fill the body. Terms drift: warning level / trigger / operating point; high-flow level / Q95; seed rule / strict rule / gain rule / E1b rule.

All 8 figures and 18 tables are numbered, captioned and cited in the text. Figures 4 and 5 are illegible at print size (axis and label text of about 3-4 pt on PDF p.18). Figure 2 shows stale facts (3 seeds, 189 sets, USGS 15-min Jan-Jun 2012), which the caption only partly discloses. Figure 7 (map) has no scale bar, north arrow, coordinate frame or data source. Captions rarely state units or sources. Table 1's 'Primary datasets' cell is noisy with '(login: no ...)' repeated 11 times.

Registry-driven numbers agree everywhere checked. Inconsistencies: the onset is defined two ways (2.3: 'first day above the level'; 4.2 and the code: target day high while the river was at or below the level k days earlier, which is why 951 and 1,116 onsets appear at 2 and 3 days); 951 also names a different quantity in 2.1; the +33.1 / +33.7 labelling; the E4e CAUTION against the 'NOT YET everywhere' wording; the abstract's 'two simple models' against four baselines; '(Section 3.1)' cited as the evidence for the engine fixes; 'the proposal's three assumptions are answered in Section 9.1', where 9.1 answers RQs, not assumptions.

Very transparent: Claude Code wrote and ran all code, AI agents reviewed it, 0 of 4 team checks, literature unread. However, the template declaration to be signed says 'Any AI-generated assistance has been reviewed', which contradicts 0 of 4 checks. The teammates' Flood_Cloud_Model package has no AI-use statement ('belongs to its authors'). No model or version is named. Members' contributions are thin and lie outside the reported pipeline, and the examiner will notice.

must_fix.proposed_text: Deep-learning rainfall-runoff models score well in simulation, but no study has priced what the day stamp of the daily rain table costs a one-day flood warning on small basins. We ask what limits a warning issued at local midnight one to three days ahead: the kind of model, or the information available at the issue time. One long short-term memory (LSTM) network shared by 12 CAMELS-US basins (south-eastern United States, 1980-2014) forecast daily flow and warned when the forecast crossed the basin's 95th-percentile flow; ridge regression and a random forest received the same inputs. Each added input was tested against a matched control, the test years 2005-2014 (611 flood onsets) were scored once, and success criteria were fixed in advance (GO: at least 70% of onsets warned, at most 30% false). With the rain table and the river gauge the LSTM's median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) was 0.59 against 0.56 for the best simple model (no clear difference), and it warned of 19% of onsets one day ahead (59% false). AORC rain to midnight (an analysis made after the fact) raised this to 52% (hindsight at most about 4 points) while its control stayed at 18%; real-time Stage IV rain in its place gave 48% (a check on the test years, not a service); the GEFS reforecast gave 38% and 37% at two and three days; a perfect weather forecast gave 64%, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice. The simple models gained as many onsets as the LSTM. On the 2010-2014 split (comparable only inside it) the river's hourly state at the issue time raised onsets warned from 39% to 47%, and to 68% with within-day rain and the forecast. Key innovation: each product's day end was measured, not assumed, and priced with matched-window controls. Limitations: no realistic input met GO (NOT YET); 12 humid basins; AORC is not real-time; the team's own checks are not yet done. [about 320 words: count before use; numbers via {{num:}} tokens]

must_fix.issue: By the rule fixed in advance (CSI >= 0.40 without GO = CAUTION), the full E4e model (lstm_wqaWHF_s: 68% warned, 39% false, onset CSI 0.47; registry e4e_wqawhf_s_l1_plain_test_verdict_onset = CAUTION, likewise at the csi and far_cap levels and for the 2-hour variant) is CAUTION for onsets one day ahead. The report repeatedly says 'NOT YET for onsets in every set that could be had in practice', which is an internal inconsistency an examiner can find in Table 6.

GO is not met.' Elsewhere replace 'NOT YET for onsets in every set that could be had in practice, at every lead' with 'GO for onsets in no set that could be had in practice: NOT YET on the main split, CAUTION for the full E4e model one day ahead on the satellite-era split (comparable only inside it)'.

must_fix.location: 9.1 RQ2 (sentences starting 'The river's hourly state (E4e...' and 'Supported for AORC...'); 7.4 Table 7 row RQ2
must_fix.issue: The gain rule fixed in advance (every seed above every seed) fails with five seeds. 9.1 nonetheless counts the hypothesis as supported 'by the paired onsets rather than the strict rule'. The registry note marks the paired counts as a description, not a test, so this relaxes the rule after the fact.
must_fix.proposed_text: The river's hourly state (E4e, satellite-era split, comparable only inside it) lifts the onsets warned from 39% to 47%, but the rule fixed in advance holds with three seeds and not with five, so by that rule the gain is not established; the paired onsets (45 warned only with the columns, 17 only without) point the same way but were not a pre-specified test. Supported for AORC and for the forecast at two and three days; not established for the river's hourly state; not supported for ERA5, the within-day rain or the one-day forecast.
